Assigned articles and book chapters with DOIs are linked directly below. Readings without DOIs are available in the [Course Files Folder](https://bruinlearn.ucla.edu/courses/239524/files).

Class meets on **Mondays from 3:00 p.m. to 5:50 p.m.** in **Public Affairs Building Room 2325**.

**Analytic Memos:** Weekly memos (500–1000 words) are due **Sundays by 5:00 p.m. PT** (Weeks 1–10) via Bruin Learn Assignments. Each memo should reference at least four readings total, including at least one from Part 1 and at least one from Part 2.

## Week 1: Networks As Theory and Perspective

### Mon., Sep. 28
*Note: Analytic Memo 1 due Sunday, Sep. 27 by 5:00 p.m. PT via Bruin Learn.*

#### Part 1: Structural Foundations & Network Theory

## Week 2: Brokerage and Intermediation

### Mon., Oct. 5
*Note: Analytic Memo 2 due Sunday, Oct. 4 by 5:00 p.m. PT via Bruin Learn.*

#### Part 1: Weak Ties, Brokerage Roles, and Mediation
- Granovetter, M. S. (1973). The Strength of Weak Ties. *American Journal of Sociology*, 78(3), 1360–1380. [link](https://doi.org/10.1086/225469)
  - *(Optional)* Rejection letter from *American Sociological Review* of the first (1969) version of the paper. [pdf](https://scatter.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/10/granovetter-rejection.pdf)
  - *(Optional)* Granovetter, M. S. (1969). Alienation Reconsidered: The Strength of Weak Ties. Reprinted in *Connections* 5(2): 4-16. [pdf](https://assets.noviams.com/novi-file-uploads/insna/Connections_Archive/1982_Volume_5__Issue_2-b2c89e8d.pdf)
- Kim, M., & Fernandez, R. M. (2023). What Makes Weak Ties Strong? *Annual Review of Sociology*, 49(1), 177–193. [link](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-soc-030921-034152)
- Gould, R. V., & Fernandez, R. M. (1989). Structures of Mediation: A Formal Approach To Brokerage In Transaction Networks. *Sociological Methodology*, 89–126. [link](https://doi.org/10.2307/270949)
- Obstfeld, D., Borgatti, S. P., & Davis, J. (2014). Brokerage As a Process: Decoupling Third Party Action From Social Network Structure. *Research In The Sociology of Organizations*, 40, 135-159. [link](https://doi.org/10.1108/S0733-558X(2014)0000040007)
- Stovel, K., & Shaw, L. (2012). Brokerage. *Annual Review of Sociology*, 38, 139-158. [link](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-soc-081309-150054)

#### Part 2: Structural Holes, Embeddedness, and Information Bandwidth
- Burt, R. S. (2004). Structural Holes and Good Ideas. *American Journal of Sociology*, 110(2), 349-399. [link](https://doi.org/10.1086/421787)
- Goldberg, A., Srivastava, S. B., Manian, V. G., Monroe, W., & Potts, C. (2016). Fitting In Or Standing Out? The Tradeoffs of Structural and Cultural Embeddedness. *American Sociological Review*, 81(6), 1190-1222. [link](https://doi.org/10.1177/0003122416671873)
- Aral, S., & Van Alstyne, M. (2011). The diversity-bandwidth trade-off. *American Journal of Sociology*, 117(1), 90-171. [link](https://doi.org/10.1086/661238)
